lever_groups.label: Taxes
lever_groups.blurb: Who pays, and how much the state collects.

lever_groups.label: Money and credit
lever_groups.blurb: The price of credit and the safety of the bank.

lever_groups.label: Climate and energy
lever_groups.blurb: Pricing and capping emissions, subsidising green investment, and getting ready for fires and droughts.

lever_groups.label: Nature and commons
lever_groups.blurb: Sharing the land and how much may be harvested.

metric_hint.gpi: Genuine progress: output adjusted for social and environmental costs
metric_hint.unemployment: Share of the labour force without a job
metric_hint.avg_income: Total household income per person per month, children and retired people included
metric_hint.median_income: The middle person: half the town earns more, half less. Compare with the average to see skew
metric_hint.debt: Government debt relative to a year of output
metric_hint.wage_share: Share of income paid as wages
metric_hint.emissions: Net emissions in the latest month: sources minus the forest sink. Open "how?" for the turn total, the accumulated total and the sources.
metric_hint.budget: Share of the carbon budget not yet used
metric_hint.temperature: Degrees C above the starting level
metric_hint.forest: Forest stock, as a share of its maximum
metric_hint.forest_health: How much of the forest is still standing and healthy. Fires burn it down; burnt tiles regrow slowly.
metric_hint.commons_health: Health of the shared land. Droughts and over-harvesting wear it down.
metric_hint.farm_health: How well the farm can produce. It follows forest and commons health and drops in a drought.
metric_hint.climate_stress: Rises as the carbon budget runs down. The more stress, the likelier and fiercer fires and droughts become.
metric_hint.gini: 0 is perfectly equal, 1 is one person has everything
metric_hint.top_wealth_share: Share of all household net worth held by the single richest household
metric_hint.legitimacy: Public trust in government; at zero the town collapses

finance_hint.revenue.wageTax: Income tax: charged on the wages households earn (the lever key is still tax_wage).
finance_hint.revenue.profitTax: Profit tax: charged on a firm's profit each month, before dividends are paid out to its owners.
finance_hint.revenue.capitalTax: Capital tax: charged on income from owning things (dividends, rent, interest) that households receive.
finance_hint.bank-cr: Equity over loans. Must stay above the limit, or lending stops.
finance_hint.bank-head: How much more the bank can lend before it hits the capital limit.
finance_hint.hh-save: Share of income left after tax, rent, loan payments and spending.
finance_hint.f-rev: Money received for purchases, from the ledger. Up to about 10% below the model's own firm revenue: a firm buying from itself moves no money.

capital_gauge.breach: Below the limit: the bank cannot lend.

misc.gst_reason: Households buy goods and services untaxed: the model taxes income, profit, capital, wealth and carbon, but a sales tax would need a price-and-purchase layer it does not have. Government revenue therefore has no GST line.
misc.energy_unit_help: {unit}: energy per month, in megawatt-hours. The unit is a label from the game's settings; the numbers are the model's own.

inspect.fire_station_effect: fires there burn shorter and spread less
inspect.planned_queued: Cancel it from the pending list to get half the political capital back.
inspect.planned_draft: Cancel it from the plan tray.
inspect.empty: Pick a building or a road in the build palette to place one here.
inspect.road: A commute over a road tile takes less time than over open ground.
inspect.firm_inactive: No firm has been founded here yet. Firms open when households move up in class.
inspect.commons: Change access and harvest in the policy drawer.
inspect.building: Removal is queued like any move and costs political capital.
inspect.forest_burning: Burning forest stops absorbing carbon. A fire station nearby shortens fires and slows their spread.
inspect.forest_regrowing: Burnt tiles regrow slowly and then stand again.
inspect.forest_standing: Forests are fixed scenery in this version.
inspect.palette_fire_station: Covers forest within about {radius} tiles: shorter, slower fires.
inspect.palette_fire_station_help: Click free ground, ideally next to the forest. Forest within about {radius} tiles burns for a shorter time and spreads less; a ring on the map shows the cover. Esc to stop.

crisis.bank_failed_detail: Its equity ran out. Savers may lose part of their deposits unless the government bails it out (a bailout also costs legitimacy).
crisis.commons_collapsed_detail: The shared land is exhausted. Farm output is likely to suffer.
crisis.fire_detail: Burning forest stops absorbing carbon, so emissions rise, and smoke harms wellbeing nearby. Fires burn out after a few months.
crisis.drought_detail: The commons and the farm suffer and food prices may rise.
crisis.low_legitimacy_title: Collapse warning: legitimacy is very low
crisis.low_budget_title: Collapse warning: carbon budget nearly spent

weather.health_forest: Share of the forest still standing. Fires burn it and the carbon sink shrinks with it.
weather.health_commons: Health of the shared land. Droughts and over-harvesting wear it down.
weather.health_farm: How well the farm can produce: it follows forest and commons health, and falls in a drought.
weather.stress_none: No climate stress yet: erratic weather begins when {onset} of the carbon budget is left.
weather.stress_active: Weather is more erratic and fires and droughts are likelier. Full stress at {full} budget left.
weather.forecast_none: No climate stress yet, so no fires or droughts are expected.
weather.forecast_quiet: Nothing unusual is expected this quarter.
weather.forecast_adapt: A fire station near the forest and resilience spending both lower the risk.
weather.lens_note: Per-tile chance that a fire starts there this month, from the simulation. The colours are scaled to the riskiest tile.

story.stress_never: Climate stress never began: the town kept more than {onset} of its carbon budget, so there were no fires or droughts.
story.budget_onset: The carbon budget fell to {onset} left, where climate stress starts, by {when}
story.budget_full: and to {full} left, where stress is at its fullest, by {when}
story.budget_never: The carbon budget never fell low enough to start climate stress ({used} used at the end).

lobby.note: You set {set}; lobbying is expected to leave about {expected} in force (this opposes the change).

system_cards.tagline: Owners keep the profits; wages follow the labour market.

facts.label: Wages
facts.value: Set by the market (a reserve army of unemployed holds them down)

system_cards.resistance: Not described in the design doc.

tradeoffs.label: Strength
tradeoffs.value: Fast growth driven by profit and investment (the growth loop in the design doc).

tradeoffs.label: Cost
tradeoffs.value: Growth also drives emissions up, and wealth can capture policy through lobbying.

system_cards.tagline: Owners still profit, but wages have a higher floor and lobbying is capped.

facts.label: Wages
facts.value: Market wages with a higher floor

facts.label: Unlocks
facts.value: A campaign-spending cap and community management of the commons

tradeoffs.label: Strength
tradeoffs.value: Unlocks the campaign-spending cap and community management of the commons, and lowers the ceiling on lobbying. The emissions cap works in every system.

tradeoffs.label: Cost
tradeoffs.value: A long transition with some output lost while it lasts.

tradeoffs.label: Trade-off
tradeoffs.value: Lower GDP growth than market capitalism, in return for a better chance of staying inside the carbon budget (a design target, not a promise).

system_cards.tagline: Employees share the surplus and own the firms.

facts.label: Wages
facts.value: A share of surplus, with a floor

facts.label: Credit
facts.value: Banks distrust co-ops: a spread is added

system_cards.resistance: High resistance. The doc does not say from whom; expect owners and lenders.

tradeoffs.label: Strength
tradeoffs.value: Profits go to workers, which pulls inequality down, and lobbying power is lowest.

tradeoffs.label: Cost
tradeoffs.value: A long transition with some output lost while it lasts; workers need training.

tradeoffs.label: Trade-off
tradeoffs.value: Slower growth, and not a free pass on emissions.
